newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil shares end up 0.29 pct in calm trading.
newsitem.headline: Brazil shares end up 0.29 pct in calm trading.

text.p: Brazil shares ended up 0.29 percent on a technical correction with investors rolling over positions in moderate trading, brokers said.
The Bovespa index of the 49 most traded shares ended up 194 points at 66,453 points with a turnover of 410.4 million reais ($398.5 million).

The bourse is expected to continue rising early next week on continued correction, they said. However traders said as November comes to an end, speculation on the country's trade deficit would likely weigh on stock prices.

Among big winners, Sao Paulo state bank Banespa common shares jumped 40 percent to close at 4.90 reais on news that a deal allowing the federal government to take over the bank could be announced next week.
Banespa's preferred shares also rose 39.13 percent to close at 4.90.
Benchmark Telebras preferred shares closed at 78.80 reais, up 0.51 percent. Mining giant Vale do Rio Doce preferred shares ended up 0.66 percent at 21.49 reais.
Oil monopoly Petrobras preferred shares rose 2.15 percent to close at 141.99 reais after the company announced reserves of 1.3 billion barrels at its new Roncador basin well.
Power utility Eletrobras preferred shares dropped 2.32 percent to close at 337 reais on technical correction, traders said.
